name: ui
description: Flexbox-style layout, builders, slots, and interactive button primitives
postInstallNotes:
## ui installed

Declarative flexbox-ish layout with builders. Compose UI like this:
```csharp
var layout = new AutoLayoutBuilder(world, viewportManager);
layout.CreateRoot(ScreenAnchor.Center)
    .Direction(LayoutDirection.Vertical)
    .Gap(40)
    .AddSlot(slot => slot.Attach(titleEntity).MeasureWith(MeasureText))
    .AddSlot(slot => slot.Attach(button1).MeasureWith(_ => button1Size))
    .Build();
```

Pipeline order (UI lives in the screen's update path):
1. `IntrinsicSizingSystem` — measure content via callbacks.
2. `AutoLayoutSystem` — compute and apply positions.
3. Your interaction systems (hover, click).
4. `ButtonMeshPrepSystem` — paint button outlines via `IMeshGenerator` (the mesh primitives ship in `rendering`).
5. `LayoutDebugSystem` — optional outline visualization (toggle `LayoutDebugSystem.Enabled`).

**Exclusive panels** (tabs, settings pages, wizard steps) are one primitive: list the panel ROOT entities in a `PanelGroupComponent` and register `PanelGroupSystem` after everything that writes their positions (notably `AutoLayoutSystem`) and before `HierarchySystem`. It PARKS the inactive panels off-screen — alive, laid out, measured — and restores the active one to the exact position it left; `Active = PanelGroupComponent.None` parks them all (a closed menu). Never hide panels instead: `VisibleComponent` does nothing on the UI/HUD/Scroll targets and un-preps the panel on Main.

**Note:** `ButtonInteractionSystem` is **not** in this module — it's game-specific (it dispatches to your selected screen/scene). Copy the pattern from `MonoDreams.Examples/System/UI/ButtonInteractionSystem.cs`.
